title: Patient Care Desk Guidance: Vacation Override Ceiling and the Patient's Prescription Insurance
content:
For a travel refill of a Kestrel Prescriptions record, the vacation override ceiling is the number of days from which the vacation override days supply is worked down. It follows the patient's active prescription coverage held under Prescription Insurance on File.

## The rule

- A plan that allows **exactly one** vacation override a plan year **and** pays claims of **90 days or more** gives a ceiling of **60 days**.
- A plan that allows **no** vacation override, **or** pays claims of **fewer than 90 days**, gives that plan's claim day limit.
- Any other plan, or no active plan, gives the class's largest vacation override days supply (90 days for a Non-Controlled Maintenance Prescription, 30 days for a Schedule V Controlled Prescription or a Specialty Limited-Distribution Prescription).

The plan's vacation override allowance and its claim day limit are read from the active coverage record. The days on hand and the owed days are then taken off the ceiling.

## Decision table (hypothetical active plans)

| Vacation overrides the plan allows a plan year | Plan's claim day limit | Ceiling |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 90 | 60 |
| 1 | 100 | 60 |
| 1 | 89 | 89 (fewer than 90) |
| 0 | 90 | 90 (the plan allows none) |
| 0 | 34 | 34 |
| 2 | 90 | the class's largest vacation override days supply |
| no active plan | — | the class's largest vacation override days supply |

## Points of judgement

**A plan allows one override but pays only 30-day claims.** It pays claims of fewer than 90 days, so the ceiling is the claim day limit, 30.

**A plan allows two overrides and pays 90-day claims.** It is neither of the first two cases, so the ceiling is the class figure — 90 days on a Non-Controlled Maintenance Prescription.
